intent: Replace blind coordinate tapping with element-targeted Android automation, shared across every repo with an Android surface, so an agent driving a phone cannot mistake a mis-tap or an unlanded keystroke for success.
scope: meta/requirements.txt + .pre-commit-config.yaml: defusedxml, needed for XML parsing under ruff S314 and on pylint's isolated path
Non-goal: MCP wrapper, scroll_to(), and rollout to ~/todo and ~/dufs-cloud/app
changes: AndroidUi driver over adb + uiautomator dump: find/find_all/wait_for/tap/type_into/type_into_field/editable_fields/dismiss_keyboard/keyboard_is_up/current_focus, every action re-resolving the element immediately before acting
Ambiguity is an error: a query matching 0 or >1 elements raises instead of acting on the first match
Typing is verified (re-reads the field, raises if unchanged) and clears first, so a filled field is replaced rather than appended to

keyboard_is_up() via dumpsys input_method, so 'element absent' and 'element behind the keyboard' are distinguishable; tap dismisses first; dismiss_keyboard uses ESCAPE then BACK and raises if the keyboard survives
Partial dumps retried with backoff; empty EditText nodes kept despite having no label at all
Fixed a real _escape bug found by its own test: backslash was inside the escape loop, so '&' became '\\&' and a password containing metacharacters would have been typed wrong

risks: A widget with no accessibility label cannot be targeted at all — workout_app's Settings gear is one. The tool surfaces the gap rather than hiding it; the fix is a Semantics(label:) in the app.
Scrolling is not modelled, so a widget outside the viewport is absent from the tree and reads as 'not found'. Callers must scroll first until scroll_to() exists.
The partial-tree heuristic (>4 labelled nodes) could in principle mis-classify a genuinely tiny screen as partial; it only costs retries, never a wrong action.
